candidate.title: TruSeq Custom Amplicon
candidate.scope: The single TruSeq Custom Amplicon product-preparation schematic: double-stranded DNA with a region of interest, addition of two custom probes, extension and ligation, addition of sequencing primers, and PCR to a product ready for cluster generation. This is a schematic-level architecture with no separately identified protocol version or alternative branch. Cluster generation and sequencing are downstream interfaces, not depicted operations.

states.label: Double-stranded DNA containing the region of interest
features: Two parallel DNA strands are drawn at the top; the next drawing highlights the region of interest in dark blue within longer light-blue strands.
The region-of-interest drawing annotates the input rather than depicting a separate chemical transformation.

evidence.locator: Upper two DNA drawings labeled Double-stranded DNA and Region of interest

states.label: DNA template with Custom Probe 1 and Custom Probe 2 at the target boundaries
features: Custom Probe 1 is drawn as a short green segment at the left boundary and Custom Probe 2 as a short magenta segment at the right boundary of the dark-blue target interval.
The underlying template is drawn as one continuous line at this stage; strand separation is not separately labeled.

evidence.locator: Custom Probe 1 / Custom Probe 2 drawing beside Add custom probes

states.label: Continuous target-containing extension and ligation product on the template
features: A continuous upper strand spans the dark-blue target interval between the green and magenta probe segments.
The longer light-blue template remains drawn beneath the shorter target-containing product.

evidence.locator: DNA drawing beside Extension and ligation

states.label: Target-containing product with sequencing primers positioned at opposite ends
features: The dark-blue target-containing molecule is flanked by green and magenta segments with angled primer extensions.
The left primer is labeled Index 1 and P7; the right primer is labeled Index 2 and P5.

evidence.locator: Angled primer drawing beside Add sequencing primers, including P7, Index 1, Index 2 and P5 labels

states.label: PCR library product ready for cluster generation
features: The final linear product retains a central dark-blue target-derived interval.
In the displayed final orientation, P5 and Index 2 lie to the left of the insert; Index 1 and P7 lie to its right.
Index identities and P5/P7 terminal segments are labeled, but no index sequences or sample assignments are supplied.

evidence.locator: Bottom library drawing labeled P5, Index 2, Index 1 and P7, beside Product ready for cluster generation

operations.label: Add custom probes
operations.description: Add Custom Probe 1 and Custom Probe 2 to the DNA; the resulting drawing places them at opposite boundaries of the region of interest on the template. The two-strand input is represented by one template line at this stage, without a separately captioned strand-separation operation.
operations.information_effect: The two custom probes define the boundaries of the DNA interval carried forward in the depicted targeted workflow; the figure does not measure targeting specificity.

evidence.locator: Arrow from Region of interest to the Custom Probe 1 / Custom Probe 2 drawing and Add custom probes caption

operations.label: Extension and ligation
operations.description: Convert the two separated probe elements on the template into a continuous strand spanning the target interval and connecting the green and magenta ends. The product is drawn on the longer template.
operations.mechanism: The source groups extension and ligation into one transformation; it shows continuity across the interval after this step and does not identify enzymes or individual reaction intermediates.
operations.information_effect: The selected target interval is represented in the newly formed target-containing DNA strand, physically linked between the probe ends.

evidence.locator: Downward arrow from the separated custom-probe drawing to the continuous strand beside Extension and ligation

operations.label: Add sequencing primers
operations.description: Add primers at the ends of the target-containing extension/ligation product. Angled primer extensions carry the labels Index 1/P7 on one side and Index 2/P5 on the other, preparing the product for the depicted PCR step.
operations.information_effect: The target-containing molecule is associated with the primer-borne terminal segments that appear in the final indexed library. The diagram supplies no index-to-specimen mapping.

evidence.locator: Downward arrow from Extension and ligation to the angled primer drawing beside Add sequencing primers

operations.label: PCR
operations.description: Amplify the primer-associated target-containing product to yield the library molecule shown with Index 2/P5 and Index 1/P7 terminal segments and a central target-derived interval. The final product is explicitly ready for cluster generation.
operations.mechanism: PCR is the named amplification step; the source does not subdivide it into cycles or specify reaction conditions.
operations.information_effect: The amplified DNA library is the carrier of the selected target sequence. Sequencing this library can interrogate its target-derived insert; it does not preserve the full length of the starting DNA molecule. This readout interpretation follows the repeated dark-blue target interval through the probe-defined product to the final library, rather than representing a depicted sequencing measurement.

evidence.locator: Arrow from the sequencing-primer drawing through PCR to the final Product ready for cluster generation drawing
Dark-blue Region of interest in the input and retained dark-blue interval in the bottom library product
evidence.rationale: The same colored target interval is retained through extension/ligation and the final PCR product, whereas the longer light-blue input flanks are not drawn in the library. This supports target-sequence representation by an amplified DNA insert; it does not establish actual read coverage, assay specificity or original-molecule counting.
